reason:
Measured with a MutationObserver over every live region ([role=status],[role=alert],[role=log],[aria-live]) across one +7 press at 1440x960, owner-editing. There are exactly three live regions; two mutate on the press: .b-undo at t=55.7ms -> 'Send the invitations moved 7 days later.UndoCtrl Z', and .b-stepRead at t=55.8ms -> 'Saturday 15 August 2026 · in 30 days'. So the mechanism is real. But it is the case the brief excludes: two DIFFERENT facts announced once each, not one change heard twice. The undo bar states the delta and that the move is reversible; the readout states the resulting absolute date. Verified directly: /2026|August|Saturday/ does not match the undo bar's text at any point, so the two never overlap in content. Nothing is repeated.

The fix is factually wrong and would make the artifact worse. It says the readout can lose role=status because it is 'the aria-describedby target the date field already points at'. It is not. Measured: #b-edit-date has aria-describedby='b-edit-when-hint', which resolves to .b-ceiling, the (empty) refusal hint; describedbyIsStepRead === false, and .b-stepRead carries no id at all. The four stepper buttons have fixed accessible names ('Move a week later', etc.) and never change. So with role=status removed, NOTHING would speak the resulting date on a stepper press: a blind owner would hear only 'moved 7 days later' — a delta with no anchor — which is the unanchored-time defect the round notes say a prior round already paid for. That is a regression, not a fix, and there is no compensating gain because the readout announces a fact no other region carries.

The keycap half is also wrong on its own mechanism. role=status carries an implicit aria-atomic=true, so when .b-undoText changes the AT walks up to the nearest aria-atomic ancestor and presents that node's ENTIRE contents. aria-live='off' on .b-undoAct and the <kbd> governs only changes ORIGINATING inside those subtrees; it does not exempt them from an atomic ancestor's presentation. The proposed attributes would therefore not remove 'Undo Ctrl Z' from the announcement at all — the fix does not do what it claims. Separately, the keycap being read is defensible rather than defective: the bar genuinely appears (it is visibility:hidden at rest, measured) and its offer is genuinely re-armed on each change, so naming the affordance and its shortcut is information for the one user who cannot see it arrive; the gate already asserts 'it names a key'.

Refuted on three independent grounds: the discriminator the brief sets (different facts, once each), a false factual premise about aria-describedby, and a fix whose stated ARIA mechanism does not hold.
